_comment: Dates are taken from what the commentaries themselves state. Where a commentary does not date its text, the entry is 'unresolved' and stays undated - the ledger prints those in a separate bucket rather than ordering them on a guess. Resolving one means finding the date in the commentary (or writing it into the commentary from the source), not recalling it. Volume order is never a proxy for composition order.

entries.note: Not a work of one date. Every text and supplement in the volume carries its own date in the commentary, printed under its heading; 87 dated blocks running from ca. 1920 to 1937. The strata below are the texts the current records cite, so a unit can carry the layer it belongs to; add a stratum as a pass reaches a further text rather than dating the volume as a whole. This is the Hua IV rule applied to a manuscript collection.

The stratified entry that makes the rest of this file worth maintaining. Hua IV is not one date: a 1912 draft, Husserl's 1915 rework, two Stein copies, a Landgrebe typescript, and four years of Husserl's insertions into it. A unit extracted from Ideas II should carry the stratum it belongs to whenever the commentary assigns it one; dating the whole volume 1912 - or 1952, its publication - flattens exactly the development the ledger exists to show.

entries.note: Only two manuscripts in the covered range are dated in the commentary, both to 1911. Part I and the body of Part II carry no date, so no unit from them should be given a stratum; § 5 places the 1908/09 ethics lectures (Hua XXVIII) already in the past, which bounds them from below but is not a date. An earlier pass recorded this entry as unresolved on the strength of the opening alone; the dates are further into the text.

Husserl's additions and marginal remarks in the Landgrebe version are a later layer that the volume's apparatus records but does not date; no stratum is given for them here. The second transcription the edition collates is not named in the material consulted, so nothing is recorded of it - in particular, the Stein strata carried by husserliana-4-ideas-ii-commentary are still not copied across.
